verdicts.question: Which languages do Bengaluru's likely pilot wards (Yeshwanthpur, Peenya, Malleshwaram, Rajajinagar, Mathikere) speak and read (census and local data), and how large is the share who can read numbers but not words? Do Bengali, Marathi and Urdu readers in India prefer international digits or native-script digits in apps and prices?
verdicts.problems: Checked on 30 Sep 2026 with WebSearch exhausted (200/200) and every cited host except raw.githubusercontent.com and microsoft.com refused (connection failed, not a 403), so most sources could only be checked locally or not at all. CONFIRMED by opening the page or file: (1) CLDR bn.xml has defaultNumberingSystem=beng, mr.xml=deva, ur_IN.xml=arabext, and ur.xml has NO defaultNumberingSystem (falls back to Latin) - opened on raw.githubusercontent.com; Node in this repo (v22.22.2, ICU 78.2, CLDR 48 - not 'Node 24' as the answer says) prints bn '১,২৩৪.৫০', mr '₹१,२३४.५०', ur '₹1,234.50' and ur-IN '₹۱٬۲۳۴٫۵۰', exactly as claimed. (2) Medhi, Sagar, Toyama ICTD 2006 (opened the PDF): three Bangalore slums, 'no fewer than 80 women and men', and the design principle 'Avoid text (but using numbers may be okay) ... subjects could easily recognize numerals (0,1,2,3,4...), these numerals can remain in the UI (at least for certain target users)'. (3) Medhi et al. ToCHI Vol 18 No 1, April 2011 (opened the PDF): 90 subjects in India, Kenya, the Philippines and South Africa; on M-PESA receipts 'almost all could identify the numbers and what they meant'. The two verbatim quotes the answer attributes to this work ('functionally illiterate or semiliterate but partially numerate' and 'many nonliterate people can read numerical digits') were NOT found in the extracted text - not confirmed by snippet, though the substance is supported. (4) The app really ships 12 locales including bn, mr and ur (src/i18n/locales.ts) and nothing sets numberingSystem today. NOT CONFIRMED by any snippet or page: the Census 2011 mother-tongue shares (Kannada 42.05%, Tamil 16.34%, Telugu 13.73%, Urdu 13.00%, Hindi 4.64%, Malayalam ~3.2%, Marathi ~2.1%) and the 50.6% migrant share; Bengaluru Urban literacy 87.67% (men 91.01%, women 84.01%); NFHS-5 women 73% / men 85%; the 2022 IJLE study with 49 Bengali migrants; ASER 2023's 25% and 43.3%; the CIS-A2K page of 24 Sep 2022; the ward histories. ARITHMETIC ERROR: the decision says kn, en, hi, ta, te and ur cover '94% of the city's mother tongues', but the answer's own shares sum to 89.76% (42.05+16.34+13.73+13.00+4.64); English as a mother tongue is never quantified, so 94% is unsupported - say 'about 90%'. '1 in 8 adults' does follow from 87.67% (12.33%). UNVERIFIABLE FIGURES: the newspaper digit counts (Anandabazar 66 vs 4, Loksatta 151 vs 68, Inquilab 43 vs 10, 'on 30 Sep 2026') are the researcher's own tallies with no snippet and cannot be reproduced on this machine; treat them as anecdote, not evidence. HIDDEN RISK the answer missed: localeMeta maps ur to hreflang 'ur-IN'; if any formatter is ever handed that tag instead of the bare 'ur', Urdu prices flip to Arabic-Indic digits (confirmed with Node) - which makes the proposed numberingSystem 'latn' pin and ASCII-digit test essential, not optional. REFINED CHAIN: the answer only covers price level L1 (household to kabadiwala). Yards, pre-processors, compounders, manufacturers, brands with EPR duties and TSDFs are registered businesses whose staff read English or Kannada and handle invoices, KSPCB category codes and yields; Latin digits and English technical names are unambiguous there, and the native-digit question is moot above L1. The 'app does all arithmetic' rule must extend to yield maths on every processing record (main output + by-products + residual = input mass) and to L2-L5 per-kg totals.
verdicts.correction: Keep the language list and the Latin-digit decision, with these changes: (1) say kn, en, hi, ta, te and ur cover about 90% of Bengaluru's 2011 mother tongues (the cited shares sum to 89.76%; English is unquantified), not 94%. (2) Mark the Census 2011, NFHS-5, ASER 2023, IJLE 2022 and CIS-A2K figures as 'not re-confirmed on 30 Sep 2026 - hosts unreachable', and drop the newspaper digit counts or label them as an unreproducible spot check. (3) What is confirmed: CLDR/ICU defaults are bn=beng, mr=deva, ur-IN=arabext, ur=latn (files opened 30 Sep 2026; Node 22.22.2 in this repo reproduces the exact strings); Medhi et al. ICTD 2006 found Bangalore slum users 'could easily recognize numerals' so digits may stay in a text-free UI; ToCHI 2011 found Kenyan M-PESA users who could not read the receipt text still 'could identify the numbers and what they meant'. (4) Pin numberingSystem 'latn' in the next-intl formats and add the ASCII-digit test for bn/mr/ur money strings; also add a test that formatting with the hreflang tag 'ur-IN' still yields Latin digits, since ur-IN defaults to Arabic-Indic. (5) Refined chain: apply icons-plus-voice-plus-Latin-digits to household, Saathi and kabadiwala screens (S0-S1, L1); above that (yard, pre-processor, compounder, manufacturer, brand, TSDF) use English technical names with KSPCB codes and let the server compute yields (main output + by-products + residual must equal input mass) and L2-L5 totals. (6) Keep the pilot-week card test, and add 10 yard or pre-processor operators to test the S0-S9 state vocabulary.

verdicts.question: Is there evidence on whether low-literacy users recognise materials faster from photos or drawn pictures? Do the SWM Rules 2026 bin colours (wet, dry, sanitary, special care) clash with a green/amber/sky palette for materials? Does the Convex React client keep unsent mutations across an offline reload, or must a weigh-and-pay queue be stored on the phone? What are the licence terms of IconScout, Blush and Icons8 illustrations for commercial apps?
verdicts.problems: Checked on 30 Sep 2026 with WebSearch exhausted and all cited hosts except microsoft.com and raw.githubusercontent.com unreachable. CONFIRMED by opening: (1) Medhi, Prasad, Toyama 'Optimal audio-visual representations for illiterate users' (Microsoft Research page): 13 health symptoms shown to 200 illiterate subjects in one of ten representations (text, static drawings, static photographs, hand-drawn animations, video, each with and without voice); main results 'richer information is not necessarily better understood overall' and 'voice annotation generally helps in speed of comprehension, but bimodal audio-visual information can be confusing'. The page dates it January 2007, 'Published by International World Wide Web Conference' (the answer says May 2007 - minor). The specific claim that static hand-drawn pictures beat photographs is not in that abstract; it is stated in the ToCHI 2011 paper ('static hand-drawn representations are better understood than photographs or ...', citing Medhi et al. 2007a) - opened and confirmed. (2) ICTD 2006 PDF opened: 'subjects were able to identify both photographs and pure cartoons, but there was a general preference for semi-abstract cartoons' and 'increase photorealism with deeper interaction' - confirmed. (3) Convex: the docs source for docs.convex.dev/client/react (overview.mdx in get-convex/convex-backend) says verbatim 'Convex React automatically retries mutations until they are confirmed to have been written to the database. The Convex backend ensures that despite multiple retries, every mutation call only executes once. Additionally, Convex React will warn users if they try to close their browser tab while there are outstanding mutations.' The installed convex 1.46.0 (dist/esm-types/browser/sync/client.d.ts) documents unsavedChangesWarning as 'Whether to prompt the user if they have unsaved changes pending when navigating away or closing a web page ... default value is true in browsers'; request_manager.js keeps inflightRequests in a JavaScript Map and no file under dist/esm/browser or dist/esm/react references localStorage or indexedDB - confirmed. registry.npmjs.org shows convex latest = 1.46.0 on 30 Sep 2026, so no newer release changes this. convex-rn README opened: 'Opt-in offline cache and mutation queue for Convex apps on React Native / Expo', 'Experimental software. Do not use this in production apps', unofficial - confirms the gap. (4) src/components/sell/family.tsx really maps paper to amber-50, plastic to sky-50, metal to muted, e-waste to brand-100 (green) and glass to a sky ring - confirmed. NOT CONFIRMED by any snippet or page: the Convex sync-page FAQ quote ('doesn't currently provide a full offline sync mechanism'); Wu et al. 2018 JEVP figures (75.9% pictures, 75.2% icons, 70.2% words; 'not allowed' items hurt); the entire SWM Rules 2026 claim - S.O. 388(E), gazetted 28 Jan 2026, in force 1 Apr 2026, PIB PRID 2219676, the CPCB 'salient features' PDF, the exact bin-colour wording (green wet, blue dry, red sanitary in public toilets) and the 'green, blue and black bins' in the return forms; the Deccan Chronicle 18 Aug 2019 BBMP story; IconScout single-end-product licence and $14.99/$19.99 prices; the Icons8 Universal Multimedia License 'effective 27 Nov 2025' and its link-credit rule; the Blush licence wording. The SWM Rules 2026 claim is the key regulatory fact behind the recolouring decision and rests on three pages none of which could be reached, so the answer cannot be passed as it stands; the practical conclusion (green means wet waste to Bengaluru households, keep green off material chips, red for reject) is sensible regardless of which rules version is current, since BBMP has used green-wet bins for years, but the citation and dates must be re-verified before they go into the plan. No arithmetic to check beyond the licence prices, which are unconfirmed. REFINED CHAIN: (a) the drawn-picture rule applies to household and kabadiwala screens (S0-S1); yards, pre-processors and compounders are literate business staff working with bales, flake, granules, black mass, slag and fly ash, where a photo plus an English name and KSPCB code is right, so the icon set needs a per-state marker for S0-S9 and a lot-type marker for main output, by-product and residual, not more drawn household objects; (b) the SWM bin palette only matters at S0-S1; state colours must not reuse family colours, and red should also mark residual lots bound for a TSDF; (c) the phone outbox is not just weigh-and-pay: Saathi pickups and sorting, yard purchases at L2/L3 and pre-processor processing records that spawn several child lots with a yield all need the same treatment, and a processing record must be one outbox entry with one client UUID plus deterministic child-lot ids so a replay creates the same lots exactly once.
verdicts.correction: Pictures: confirmed. Medhi, Prasad and Toyama (WWW 2007; 13 symptoms, 200 illiterate subjects, ten representations) found richer media is not better understood and voice speeds comprehension; the ToCHI 2011 paper restates that static hand-drawn pictures are better understood than photographs; the ICTD 2006 Bangalore study found a general preference for semi-abstract cartoons with photorealism for drill-down. Keep the decision (drawn local item + spoken name, photos in drill-down). The Wu et al. 2018 bin-signage percentages are not re-confirmed; cite them as 'pictures and icons beat words, roughly 75% vs 70%' only after someone opens the PDF. Bin colours: the SWM Rules 2026 citation (S.O. 388(E), 28 Jan 2026, in force 1 Apr 2026, PIB PRID 2219676) could not be confirmed from any page on 30 Sep 2026 and must be re-verified on egazette.gov.in or pib.gov.in before it enters the plan; the design conclusion stands on Bengaluru practice alone (green = wet, blue = dry, red = sanitary), so still take green off material chips (e-waste today uses brand-100), keep blue/sky for 'dry, recyclable', amber and a third non-bin colour for families, red only for reject, hazard and TSDF-bound residual lots. Convex: confirmed from the docs source and the installed 1.46.0 package - mutations are retried until written and run exactly once, the tab-close warning (unsavedChangesWarning, default true) exists, but the queue is an in-memory Map with no localStorage or IndexedDB, and npm latest is still 1.46.0, so an offline reload or phone restart drops unsent records; the convex.dev sync FAQ quote is unconfirmed but the conclusion does not depend on it. Build the IndexedDB outbox keyed by a client UUID with idempotent mutations, and extend it beyond weigh-and-pay to Saathi pickup/sort events, yard purchases (L2/L3) and pre-processor processing records (one entry per record, deterministic ids for the main-output, by-product and residual lots, yield computed server-side). Licences: none of the IconScout, Icons8 or Blush terms or prices could be confirmed; treat '$14.99/month annual, $19.99 monthly', 'UML effective 27 Nov 2025' and the Blush free-commercial wording as open items to be re-read on the vendor pages before purchase, and keep the fallback of the Icons8 link credit on the About screen if any free asset ships.
